Owner reports weak site performance/SEO and wants a technical-only pass -- no copy, content or visual/design changes. Scope: meta tags per page/game (title, description, canonical, Open Graph, Twitter card), structured data (JSON-LD, e.g. Game or SoftwareApplication schema), a real sitemap.xml (check whether src/app/sitemap.ts and src/app/robots.ts App Router conventions exist -- they likely do not yet -- add if missing), Core Web Vitals and Lighthouse issues (image optimization, render-blocking resources, font loading, hydration cost). Also required: full keyboard accessibility across the whole app -- every interactive element including dropdowns, menus and tabs must be reachable and operable via Tab, Shift+Tab, Enter, Escape and arrow keys, with visible focus states, correct ARIA roles/labels, and no keyboard traps. Run whatever real auditing is available first (Lighthouse, axe-core, or a manual keyboard walkthrough) to find concrete issues, then fix everything found -- do not guess at problems. Note: public/robots.txt and public/llms.txt already exist but are stale (still list hidden/removed games); they are separate pending tasks, do not rewrite them here. Explicitly out of scope this round: copy changes, visual redesign, content or keyword strategy, backlinks.

## 2026-09-29 — Technical SEO + keyboard/ARIA accessibility pass: standard vs hard, design round or not
Context: frontend P1 card, no override. SEO groundwork already exists: `src/app/layout.tsx` exports
`metadata`, `src/app/[game]/page.tsx` has `generateMetadata`, `/admin` sets `robots: noindex`; there
is no `src/app/sitemap.ts`/`robots.ts`, and `public/robots.txt` exists (a Next route and a public file
at the same path conflict, and the card forbids rewriting the txt here). `ui/Modal` already has a
focus trap + Escape. The rest of the scope is "audit first, fix everything found" across the shell,
`Navigation` (desktop links + mobile drawer), `LogInSignUp` tabs, modals and the 19 game renderers.
`hard` was defensible (whole-app breadth, new route conventions, JSON-LD); `standard` with no design
round was defensible too (one frontend area, every fix follows an existing Next/ARIA pattern).
Decision: `difficulty: standard`, `risk: low` (no auth, pipeline, protocol or settings code),
`areas: frontend/ui/games`, `needsDesignRound: true` — not for difficulty but because the spec is
long-and-vague by construction: the design round must run the Lighthouse/axe/keyboard audit and turn
its findings into numbered steps with done-checks, settle the robots.ts-vs-public/robots.txt conflict
(leave robots to the pending card; sitemap.ts only, excluding hidden games per MASTER_PLAN), and cap
game-renderer edits to GAME_DESIGN_CONSTRAINTS-safe ARIA/focus changes with no visual drift.
`engineModel: sonnet` provisional, `planModel: fable`.
Consequences: audit-driven "fix everything" cards get a design round even when single-area, since
the plan is where the vagueness gets fixed; the engine is not upgraded for breadth. Any fix that
would change visuals beyond a focus ring is out of scope and becomes a follow-up card.
